newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: YACHTING-GLOBAL CHALLENGE YACHTS REACH AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-GLOBAL CHALLENGE YACHTS REACH AUSTRALIA.

text.p: The 14 contenders in the gruelling around-the-world BT Global Challenge yacht race began arriving in Sydney late on Sunday night, race officials said.

The yacht Save the Children was first to finish the 1,230 nautical mile leg from the New Zealand capital, Wellington, arriving at 0732 GMT, followed soon after by Group 4, spokesman Alister Henderson said.
The remaining contenders were expected by 1400 GMT.

All crews in the challenge, considered one of the world's toughest around-the-world sailing races because it goes against prevailing winds, are amateurs who have paid about A$40,000 (US$30,500) each to take part.
The skippers of the 20-metre steel-built yachts are professionals.
The race takes the boats 48,000 km from Southampton, England, around the world via South America, New Zealand, Australia and Africa.
Racers are due to leave Sydney on March 2 for Cape Town.
